Sampling Protocol - Grab: (Mussels were collected by means of a dredge fitted with a 5-mm mesh net. Then, mussels of size between 30-40 mm were selected and left for 24 hours in sea water for depuration. The uppermost 5-cm layer of sediments was collected by means of a Petterson grab sampler, and kept frozen until analysis.)

Analytical Protocol - Atomic absorption spectroscopy: (Concentrations were measured using a model Video 11E Thermo Jarrel Ash atomic absorption spectrometer using either air-acetylene flame or a model CTF 188 furnace for atomization. Smith-Heftjer or D2 background correction was applied throughout the measurements. IAEA-140/TM (sea plant homogenate) and IAEA-SD-M-2/TM (marine bottom sediment) standards were analyzed. Recovery was between 93% (Fe) and 103% (Cd).)
limitations: FAAS/GFAAS used, although authors don't specify which approach for which metal. Although both are probably appropriate for assessing copper in filter feeders, due to the lack of specificity I will report this as "partly met".
Total copper is appropriate for biota sampling.
